//: Documented, INTENTIONAL dependency downgrades. scripts/check-no-downgrade.mjs fails the build if any dependency's highest resolved version in package-lock.json drops below what is on `main` — the #1903 failure class, where a lockfile regenerated from a stale base silently reverted brace-expansion 5.0.9 -> 5.0.7 and re-opened a CVE. Almost every downgrade is a mistake. The rare legitimate one (e.g. reverting a bad major that broke the build) goes here so it is never silent.
//exception-shape: Each entry: { name, from, to, reason, approvedBy, date }. An entry only wavies a downgrade whose landing version equals `to` exactly, so a stale exception cannot mask a DIFFERENT downgrade of the same package.
//why-this-file-needs-a-human: This file lives under .github/, which check-automerge-allowlist.mjs bars from content auto-merge (NEVER_ALLOWLIST). So adding a downgrade exception always requires a founder-reviewed PR — you cannot self-approve a version reversion.
